newsitem.title: USA: Texas utilities operating under winter alert.
newsitem.headline: Texas utilities operating under winter alert.

text.p: Texas utilities were asked to double spinning reserve on Monday as icy weather swept across the state, prompting the Electric Reliability Council of Texas to declare a cold weather alert, utility officials said.

Two transmission lines from the South Texas Project nuclear plant went down in a freezing rain storm overnight, but redundant systems kept the outages from affecting the statewide grid, said Sam Jones, director of the ERCOT-ISO, which monitors transmission on the statewide grid.
"There's adequate supply in the state and the transmission system is holding up well," Jones told Reuters.

A rare sleet storm accompanied by lightning and thunder swept across south Texas overnight, coating trees and power lines with a heavy sheet of ice. The arctic blast boosted residential demand statewide, but overall demand was lower than expected as schools and businesses closed for the day, Jones said.

Houston Lighting and Power Co reported 125,000 customers remained without power midday Monday as falling tree limbs snapped transmission lines in the city's northern and western suburbs. Load was higher than normal, but well below peak, a utility spokesman said.
"We have adequate generation," spokesman Graham Painter said.

One transmission line from the South Texas Project nuclear plant to the Columbus, Texas area was brought up early in the day, but crews were still working on a line connecting the plant and San Antonio, Jones said.
